brief: Own visual system, with the dynamic energy and precision of Morph and Assembly; color; PFP evaluation.

prompts.name: Ribbonfield
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / graphic generative artwork.
Create ONE original color artwork for Tincta, to be considered as a memorable X profile picture and website illustration.
Input images: the green Morph and blue Assembly images are QUALITY and ENERGY references only. Learn their mathematical precision, visual rhythm, optical movement, restraint and strong overall composition. Do not copy their shapes, nested rotating square construction, 4x4 grid, or quarter-circle tiles. This new artwork needs its OWN visual system.
Format: one centered artwork on a square pure-white canvas, occupying about 76% of the canvas and fitting safely inside a circular avatar crop. Generous clean margins. No labels, typography, logos, framing, multiple proposals, watermarks, mockups or interface.
Color: disciplined warm Tincta inks: intense vermilion #FF3300, orange #FF6600, red #FF0000 and deep oxblood #330000, with white negative space. Color rhythm should reveal the construction. Sophisticated crisp vector-like graphic artwork. Implied depth comes from geometry and overlapping color, never glossy 3D material, lighting, shadows, blur, gradients or texture.
The result should have the energy of a generative art piece and the composure of an authored cultural identity. Complex enough to reward looking, simple enough in its outer shape to remember. No torus, spirograph, rotated square tunnel, tiled checkerboard, generic flower, star/sparkle, infinity sign, letter, stock crypto emblem or literal object.
Direction A — RIBBONFIELD: a single continuous open ribbon of about 28 fine colored filaments follows an unusual asymmetric trajectory. It rises as a wide bowed fan, compresses into one tight diagonal waist, then opens sideways into a shorter sharply cut fan. The two ends point in different directions, suggesting a flowing sheet caught mid-turn. One controlled over-under passage, articulated with a clean white interruption. The dynamic comes from compression and release of parallel filaments, not uniform stripes or concentric outlines. Combine a few intense narrow solid-color folds with delicate evenly weighted lines; keep a specific compact silhouette and a conspicuous off-axis notch. It should feel fluid and tensile, not like an S, a bow tie, a knot icon, a bird or a closed loop. Avoid a bundle of thick black tubes. Draw an exceptionally elegant, precise, unfamiliar graphic form.

Direction B — FOLDSCAPE: a sculptural graphic built from a sequence of 9 or 11 sharply folded polygonal planes, stepping around an off-center spine. Develop a compact irregular silhouette with one high fan, one low terrace and an angular central white cleft. The planes fan out, fold back, and change width in a deliberate non-repeating rhythm; each plane has two flat colored faces, so the viewer can follow the folding rule. Use broad vermilion and orange faces with slim oxblood return faces and exact white seams. This is a geometric composition with tension and movement, not a radial rosette, accordion stock icon, paper bird, gem, lightning bolt or literal origami object. No outlined square frames, no tiles and no rounded quarter circles. Flat solid colors, crisp straight edges, no rendered material or shadows. Make the precise relationship between the pleats and the silhouette remarkable.

Direction C — PHASEFIELD: a lively compact field of about 100 to 180 separated solid colored circular and elongated elliptical particles. Every particle follows a precise underlying smooth vector field. The particles collectively make one unusual asymmetric shape: a broad curved crest, a compressed diagonal waist, and a shorter returning lobe. Create flowing negative-space channels through the field, with deliberate changes in particle size and spacing. Broad densely packed vermilion regions should remain visible when small, while fine orange and oxblood particles articulate the edges. The pattern must feel like a controlled wave of matter bending under a rule, not random confetti, a data chart, a galaxy, a sphere, a fingerprint, an S, an infinity loop or a halftone photo. Do not add connecting lines or trails. Keep only the flat isolated particles and white canvas, with a coherent dynamic silhouette. Show a new modular language entirely different from square tiles.
